name: Shakti arm of Tsang 2004 with coil polarity (amygdala left, LTP right, 30 min)
origin: Todd Murphy (Shakti, sound-card driven); tested by Tsang, Koren & Persinger 2004
summary: The Shakti arm of Tsang, Koren & Persinger 2004, rebuilt with the vendor's coil polarity: three coils per side (positive over the temporal lobe, reversed over the frontal and parietal lobes), the amygdala burst-firing signal on the left and the hippocampal signal on the right together, 30 min once a week for 4 weeks. The lab reported no treatment differences in delta, theta, low alpha, beta or gamma, and a session-by-treatment interaction in high alpha due mainly to Shakti.
notes: How it differs from murphy-shakti-helmet-stereo, the other rebuild of this arm: (1) the vendor's comparison page puts a positive ('north') coil over the temporal lobe and a negative ('south') one over the frontal lobe on each side, plus a parietal coil, reproduced here with weights -1 (that program drives all coils with one polarity); the parietal coil's polarity is not confirmed in the research and is driven negative, as 'one positive and two negative coils' per side in the vendor description quoted by that program; (2) the hippocampal signal is the primed burst described for the Persinger-lab 'LTP' file instead of Larson & Lynch theta bursts; (3) the sites are F3, T7, P3 and F4, T8, P4 instead of F7, T7, CP5 and F8, T8, CP6 (both are inferences from 'frontal, temporal and parietal'; CH4 and CH8 stay unused). Per the vendor page the amygdala-derived signal runs on the left and the hippocampal one on the right; here they play at the same time, with no rotation (the stereo reading murphy-shakti-helmet-stereo also uses). Both Shakti files are proprietary: the amygdala 'burstx' signal is the built-in accelerating burst (6 to 30 Hz), 230 points of 3 ms (0.69 s); the hippocampal signal is five primed bursts in 1 s (a 1-ms primer, then 4 pulses at 100 Hz from 150 ms later; Corradini 2014, Delparte & Persinger 2007; the 10-ms spacing is the 100 Hz end of the lab's "4 pulses ... between 100 and 200 Hz", which also puts the primer gap near 170 ms rather than 150 ms, Persinger 2010). Both start together every 4 s; the vendor's exact gaps are not in the research. Tsang, Koren & Persinger 2004 recorded QEEG over the left and right frontal, temporal, parietal and occipital lobes on 4 successive weeks in 12 subjects before each 30-min exposure to Shakti (Todd Murphy's device, driven from compact disc through a computer sound card), to "the set of 4 solenoids (Koren boxes) generating a burst-firing magnetic field through the temporal lobes", or to a sham field. Compared with baseline there were no treatment differences in delta, theta, low alpha, beta or gamma; a session-by-treatment interaction in high alpha (10.5-13 Hz) was "due primarily to the Shakti treatment", which the authors called "congruent with the subjective experiences reported by some users of the technology". The lab's own arm is persinger-koren-boxes-tsang-2004; run sham for the third arm. Source cautions: n = 12, one interaction among many comparisons, a single lab testing a commercial device associated with its own work; Gendle & McGrath 2012 later found no effect of the 8 Coil Shakti on emotional responses under sham control, and Granqvist 2005 found no field effect double-blind. Not for anyone with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on headache, nausea or distress.
setting: Seated or reclined, eyes closed, in a quiet, dark room. Record EEG before each session to compare with the paper.
schedule: 30 min once a week on 4 successive weeks.
source: Tsang, Koren & Persinger 2004, Int J Neurosci 114:1013 (Shakti vs Koren boxes) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15527205/ ; Murphy, Shakti Spiritual Technology & Koren Helmet - A Comparison https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/koren_shakti.htm ; Corradini 2014, MA thesis, Laurentian University (primed-burst LTP file) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/1455e1f3-2f1d-47b5-93cd-23713d69e651 ; Delparte & Persinger 2007, Int J Neurosci 117:295 ('1 s pulse of 5 trains') https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17365115/ ; Persinger 2010, NeuroQuantology 8(4):444 (the LTP pattern: a primer then 4 pulses about 170 ms later at 100-200 Hz) http://web.archive.org/web/20150426091303id_/http://www.neuroquantology.com/index.php/journal/article/download/301/346 ; Carniello 2020, PhD thesis, Laurentian University (230-point burst-firing file, 3 ms) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/8c92763c-cd19-4a21-b242-3b572a28ce55 ; Martin, Koren & Persinger 2004, Int J Neurosci 114:1259 (.wav through a coil worked, compact disc did not) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15370185/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
